definitions.gloss: making into a habit; habituation; routinization
definitions.explanation: The process of turning an action or behavior into a regular habit or routine. Can refer to both deliberately forming a habit and the natural process of something becoming routine.

examples.japanese: {運動|うんどう}を{習慣化|しゅうかんか}したい。
examples.english: I want to make exercise a habit.

examples.japanese: {毎朝|まいあさ}の{散歩|さんぽ}が{習慣化|しゅうかんか}してきた。
examples.english: My morning walks have become a habit.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{行動|こうどう}を{習慣化|しゅうかんか}するには、{少|すく}なくとも{三週間|さんしゅうかん}は{続|つづ}ける{必要|ひつよう}がある。
examples.english: To make a new behavior a habit, you need to keep it up for at least three weeks.

notes:
Composed of {習慣|しゅうかん} (habit) + {化|か} (transformation suffix, '-ization'). A popular topic in self-improvement and productivity literature in Japan.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {習慣化|しゅうかんか}する — to make into a habit; to become habitual
- {習慣化|しゅうかんか}のコツ — tips for forming habits
- {習慣化|しゅうかんか}に{成功|せいこう}する — to succeed in forming a habit
- {早起|はやお}きを{習慣化|しゅうかんか}する — to make early rising a habit

RELATED TERMS:
- {習慣|しゅうかん} — habit, custom
- {日課|にっか} — daily routine; refers to the established routine itself
- {癖|くせ} — habit (often unconscious or negative); unlike {習慣化|しゅうかんか}, not deliberately formed
- ルーティン — routine (loanword); increasingly common, especially in sports contexts
